candidates.title: Rose
candidates.one_line: The red that has already turned pink — petals, not warning lights.
candidates.covers: OKLCH h 340-15 at any chroma above the neutral floor. Dusty rose, cherry, coral-red, neon pink-red: rose(358), dusty-rose(356), chrome-rain(356), vaporwave-mall(347), dark-pastel-cotton-candy(349), vibrant-synthwave(350), void-sunset(341), vibrant-sunset(8).
candidates.risk: Read literally it promises pastel pink; the bucket also holds saturated reds (vibrant-synthwave, void-sunset), so the vivid cards look misfiled.

candidates.title: Persimmon
candidates.one_line: Ripe fruit orange: the warm end of red, before it becomes gold.
candidates.covers: OKLCH h 15-48. Vermilion, terracotta, salmon, neon orange: glitch-punk(22), dark-rosepine(23), dragon-blood(25), rice-paper(26), ares(30), red-alert(35), peach-fuzz(39), redwood(39), brutalist-concrete(39), solar-flare(40), warm-parchment(19).
candidates.risk: The fruit reads muted-autumn; the bucket's most saturated cards (glitch-punk C=0.254, ares C=0.186) are louder than the name suggests.

candidates.title: Amber
candidates.one_line: Warm gold you can see through — resin, lamplight, old paper.
candidates.covers: OKLCH h 48-72. Gold, brass, honey, cream-gold: warm-lightmode(50), nature-autumn(51), dark-pastel-peach-blossom(52), sandstone(54), ember(55), dark-cozy-paper(62), newsprint-noir(62), charizard(65), dark-lcars(66), retro-amber(70).
candidates.risk: Amber's own canonical swatch sits near h84 (brighter, more yellow) than this arc, which is the muted/dark warm gold; a colour-literate reviewer will say amber belongs one step clockwise.

candidates.title: Olive
candidates.one_line: Yellow gone dark and vegetal — khaki, brass, unlit gold.
candidates.covers: OKLCH h 72-90. Khaki, brass, dark yellow, warm cream-khaki: nature-desert(76), netrunner(76), single-malt(76), amber-terminal(77), typewriter-cream(80), desert-neon(81), dark-gruvbox(83), dark-vanilla(83), midnight-studio(83), dark-crimson(85), dark-pastel-buttercup(86), obsidian(90), sisyphus(90).
candidates.risk: Tailwind's newer 'olive' is a grey-green neutral, so users trained on it will expect desaturated green, not warm khaki; olive also implies low chroma while netrunner (C=0.170) is vivid.

candidates.title: Lemon
candidates.one_line: Acid yellow with green waiting inside it.
candidates.covers: OKLCH h 90-112. Chartreuse, acid yellow, near-white yellow: arcane-tome(90), black-canary(95), enchanted-forest(97), dark-lemon(104), white-flash(110).
candidates.risk: In English 'a lemon' means a defective unit — a quality word sneaking in through idiom; the bucket also holds near-white white-flash (L=0.97), which reads as off-white, not lemon.

candidates.title: Fern
candidates.one_line: Leaf green with the sun off it — sage, moss, forest.
candidates.covers: OKLCH h 112-150. Sage, moss, forest, pure green: dark-everforest(126), moss-stone(126), dark-sage(129), linen-sage(129), green-screen(143), cyberpunk(144), nature-forest(144).
candidates.risk: Fern is a muted leaf colour, but the bucket also carries the catalogue's most saturated green (cyberpunk, C=0.278); the name undersells it.

candidates.title: Teal
candidates.one_line: The duck's wing: green that has gone cold, blue that has gone green.
candidates.covers: OKLCH h 150-215. Seafoam, mint, cyan, deep ocean: retro-terminal(152), seafoam-silk(162), dark-pastel-mint-sorbet(164), vibrant-neon(168), hermes-teal(188), nature-ocean(195), graphite(195), deep-ocean(210).
candidates.risk: One name has to hold a 65-degree arc, so deep-ocean(210) will look blue to a user expecting teal; the widest semantic span in the set.

candidates.title: Cobalt
candidates.one_line: The blue of glass and glaze — clean, cold, unmistakably blue.
candidates.covers: OKLCH h 215-255. Sky, azure, navy, powder blue: bone-white(216), vibrant-pacific(217), dark-ayu(237), poseidon(241), dark-solarized(244), nature-nordic(244), retro-blue(245), slate-mist(245), dark-navy(249), baby-blue(249), forge-master(249), dark-mac(250), dark-pastel-powder-blue(251), slate(251), dark-vscode(252), dark-charcoal(253), dark-nord(254).
candidates.risk: Cobalt implies a deep saturated pigment; the bucket includes bone-white (C=0.060) and powder blue, and cobalt's own swatch (h~260) sits just past the arc's upper edge.

candidates.title: Indigo
candidates.one_line: Blue with the red already in it — dye, dusk, deep water.
candidates.covers: OKLCH h 255-280. Royal blue, ultramarine, blue-violet: aurora-boreal(256), high-noon(256), dark-tokyo-night(257), dark-github(258), stained-glass(258), blueprint(259), dark-catppuccin(262), nous(263), dark-one(263), daylight(263), dark-kanagawa(264), dark-material(264), alabaster(266).
candidates.risk: CSS 'indigo' is a purple (#4B0082) and Tailwind's is blue-violet; users who learned either will expect different things. This arc is the blue side.

candidates.title: Violet
candidates.one_line: Purple at its clearest — the last hue before blue gives out.
candidates.covers: OKLCH h 280-300. Purple, plum, twilight, lilac-grey: midnight(286), liquid-silver(286), dark-obsidian(290), deep-void(294), commodore-64(297), eclipse(299).
candidates.risk: Violet is a spectral hue (short-wavelength blue-violet) while this arc is purple proper; CSS violet (#EE82EE) is pale magenta-leaning, so the name and the swatch disagree.

candidates.title: Magenta
candidates.one_line: Purple that has picked up red until it hums.
candidates.covers: OKLCH h 300-340. Fuchsia, orchid, aubergine, hot pink: dark-dracula(300), lavender-dream(301), dark-plum(305), dark-aubergine(306), shadow-thief(311), neon-ghost(328).
candidates.risk: Magenta is a printing ink at maximum chroma; half this bucket is deep and muted (plum, aubergine), so the name over-promises intensity and under-describes the pinks.

candidates.title: Slate
candidates.one_line: Colour with the colour taken out — stone, ash, graphite.
candidates.covers: Achromatic: accent chroma below the neutral floor, hue irrelevant. mono(C=0.000), dark-bone(0.021), minimal-graphite(0.024), steel-thread(0.012), warm-ash(0.031).
candidates.risk: Slate is a cool blue-grey, but the bucket holds warm greys (warm-ash, dark-bone); 'Slate' quietly makes the category feel colder than its contents.

collisions.why: Olive, Fern and (weakly) Persimmon belong to the same natural-world vocabulary as the Earth pack. They name hue, not mood, so they do not duplicate the axis — but Fern is the one word that could be mistaken for a mood, and Earth-pack skins (nature-forest, moss-stone, sandstone) are exactly the cards that will appear under it. Category and pack will visibly agree on those cards, which makes the two axes look redundant.

Amber-on-black (amber-terminal, retro-amber) and teal CRT (retro-terminal, vibrant-neon) are the retro computing trope. A user may reach for the Retro pack when they mean the Amber category; the cards overlap by design but the names must not.
Magenta, Lemon and Teal are the neon triad of the cyberpunk aesthetic (glitch-punk, netrunner, neon-ghost). No name duplicates 'Cyberpunk', but three categories sit in its colour story.
Slate is the nearest category to Noir's register — both are dark and neutral. 'Slate' is a hue family, 'Noir' is a served mood, so the axes stay distinct, but on a dark card the two read similarly.
Fern and Olive carry the same quiet-green signal as Zen. Low risk because Zen is a mood and the names are plants, but a Zen card and a Fern card can be the same card.
No candidate is a synonym of 'core'. It is the default/provenance pack, and provenance words are already banned from category names, so the axes cannot collide here — listed for completeness.

The product name already occupies the colour-behaviour register. No candidate repeats it, but 'Chroma' + twelve colour words means the product name stops doing any work; category names must stay concrete nouns, not colour-abstract nouns.

Pre-existing, not introduced here: the current id 'earth' is a straight duplicate of the Earth pack. Two axes sharing one word is the exact defect this pass removes. Any migration must retire it, not map it to a new 'earthy' word.

External, not in-product: Tailwind now ships 'olive' as a grey-green neutral. Our Olive is warm khaki. Users who know Tailwind will expect desaturated green, so the chip colour and the chip name must do the explaining.

The catalogue already contains skins called 'slate', 'slate-mist', 'rose' and 'ember'. A category named Slate containing a skin named Slate is legal but redundant at the card level; 'ember' is also one letter from Amber, which is why Amber's neighbour could never be called Ember.

Violet is the one name carried over unchanged. That is deliberate — it is a hue word with no pack conflict — but its arc must shrink from the old catch-all to 280-300, or the word keeps its old meaning by accident.

rejected.title: Ember
rejected.why: Phonetic twin of Amber. In a filter row the two are indistinguishable when spoken aloud and easy to misread; one of the two had to go, and Amber has the stronger hue precedent.

rejected.title: Earthy
rejected.why: Explicitly banned: paraphrase of the Earth pack. Same for Terra, Terracotta, Clay, Soil, Loam.

rejected.title: Noir
rejected.why: Banned: duplicate of the Noir pack.

rejected.title: Cyber, Neon, Chrome
rejected.why: Collide with the Cyberpunk pack and imply intensity/mode rather than hue family.

rejected.title: Retro, Zen
rejected.why: Pack names. Any category using them would merge two axes the product deliberately separates.

rejected.title: Pastel
rejected.why: A chroma-and-lightness class, not a hue. It implies light mode, and it is one of the four character words this pass exists to remove.

rejected.title: Vibrant
rejected.why: Intensity, not hue — it overlaps every category and would either empty itself or swallow the vivid cards of all twelve.

rejected.title: Muted
rejected.why: Same failure as Vibrant, inverted; it is a rule that belongs inside each category, not a category.

rejected.title: Minimal
rejected.why: A style claim about the skin, not a measurement of its accent. Cannot be derived from a palette by any rule.

rejected.title: Warm / Cool
rejected.why: A temperature axis, not a hue family. Both span five or more categories, so either word would be a second, contradictory sort key.

rejected.title: Gold
rejected.why: Near-synonym of Amber with no reliable boundary between them; also one of the twelve deprecated ids, so keeping it would blur old and new taxonomies.

rejected.title: Stone
rejected.why: Rejected in favour of Slate: 'stone' is an Earth-pack word and would be read as a material mood rather than a chroma floor.

rejected.title: Brown
rejected.why: ISCC-NBS has it as a basic term, but in UI accents brown is a darkened orange: it would steal the muted warm cards from Persimmon and Amber and read as the Earth pack.

rejected.title: Chartreuse
rejected.why: Ten letters, French liqueur etymology, routinely misspelt and mistranslated; fails the translation and scan tests where Lemon passes.

rejected.title: The gemstone set (Garnet, Amethyst, Emerald, Sapphire, Citrine)
rejected.why: Coherent and pretty, but three to four syllables each, a jewellery-brand register, and several (Garnet, Citrine) are not stable colour terms outside English.

rejected.title: Sunset, Aurora, Dusk, Mist
rejected.why: Scenes and times of day, not hue families. Each names a gradient or a lighting condition, and all four echo the Retro/Noir mood axis.

rejected.title: Prism, Spectrum, Multi
rejected.why: Describes how many hues a skin uses, which is a different axis from which hue it uses; would need its own measured rule and would cut across all twelve.

rejected.title: Premium, Pro, Signature
rejected.why: Quality claims, not colours; forbidden by the naming principles.

rejected.title: Taupe, Mauve, Mist
rejected.why: Tailwind's low-chroma neutrals: ambiguous against Slate, hard to translate, and they describe greys that our floor already assigns to Slate.

unverified: Pack membership per skin: PALETTE-ANALYSIS.json reports pack as an empty string for all 109 cards, so every pack-collision judgement here is semantic (by name) rather than measured (by shared cards).
Whether the twelve current category ids are already translated anywhere in the product; the translation-survival claim for these names is a judgement, not a test.
Radix chromatic scale names beyond Gray/Mauve/Slate/Sage/Olive, which is all the fetched Scales page rendered; the claim that Radix names scales after hues is supported only for the neutrals.
Comprehension of 'Persimmon' outside English-speaking markets (the fruit is widely known; the colour term is not).

The exact hue cut points. The arcs in this document are descriptive of where the 109 accents actually fall, not prescribed thresholds; the rules lane owns the boundaries and may move any of them by a few degrees.
